findings.reason: The protected implementation is a compact, conventional sparse-quadtree search at an expert-interview standard. Its coordinate names, midpoint calculation, invalid-region guard, oracle pruning, singleton base case, and four disjoint recursive calls expose the complete algorithm without unnecessary state or abstraction. No material clarity, correctness, or complexity improvement warrants a candidate.

A false oracle result proves that a queried region contributes zero. A true singleton contributes exactly one because an integer coordinate holds at most one ship. Every other occupied region is partitioned at mid_x and mid_y into ordered, pairwise-disjoint children whose union is the parent, so each hidden ship enters exactly one child. Induction on inclusive rectangle size therefore proves that the recursive sum returns every in-range ship exactly once.

An independent oracle counted fixture coordinates lying in the inclusive target without using the solution's recursion. It, the protected app source, the immutable native source, and a separately written longest-side binary-partition control agreed on all eight visible cases, all 512 ship subsets of a 3-by-3 target, and 10,000 deterministic random schema-valid databases. The protected and native sources also produced identical oracle-query traces throughout.

Seed 1274 generated 10,000 legal targets including 1,667 full-grid, 1,667 vertical, 1,667 horizontal, and 1,667 minimum two-coordinate rectangles; 910 contained no in-range ship, 740 contained the maximum ten, 1,818 forced an inclusive-boundary ship, and 13,332 outside-target ship insertions exercised pruning. The protected and native sources never exceeded 341 calls, while the independent binary-partition control never exceeded 349.

The bounded-domain certificate now records the exact proof Q <= 1 + 4 sum from l = 0 to d - 1 of min(4^l, s). With s <= 10, C <= 1001, and d <= 10, the protected search makes at most 341 oracle calls, below the source limit of 400. Focused certificate validation passed. An exact point-by-point control returned the correct result with an unrestricted oracle after 441 calls on a 21-by-21 empty target, then failed only the query-budget rule at call 401 under the legal cap, confirming why scaling tiers are not the appropriate evidence.

The two authenticated source examples remain first and preserve every coordinate and output. The invented empty-map row is now correctly classified as a trial, the invalid singleton outer target was replaced by the minimum legal two-coordinate rectangle, both formerly hidden rows are visible trials, and a visible outside-only map was added. All eight ordinary cases are visible and cover no ships, one ship, the ten-ship maximum, full range, narrow geometry, inclusive boundaries, outside-target ships, and oracle pruning.

Metadata consistently identifies Premium LeetCode algorithm problem 1274, Python as the app language, and Solution.countShips as the verified native entrypoint. Fresh authenticated evidence confirms the interactive hidden Sea API, at most one ship per integer point, inclusive rectangle queries, at most ten target ships, the 400-call rejection threshold, both coordinate inequalities through 1000, blindfolded access, and distinct outer corners.

The protected app and immutable Accepted native sources have identical guards, oracle query placement, singleton detection, midpoint partition, four child rectangles, and summation; their only structural difference is the required app function and local Point/Sea equivalents versus LeetCode's class-method wrapper and injected judge models. submission.json remains bound to verified submission 2068282593, and both source files and the manifest remain unchanged.

The complete Approach matches the protected source exactly. It derives oracle pruning, the non-overlapping four-way partition, termination and exact counting, O(s log C) calls, O(log C) stack space, the exact 341-call legal-domain bound, the outer-corner versus recursive-singleton distinction, and all material alternatives and edge cases.

The modular Reference preserves the interactive model, hidden-access restriction, inclusive API semantics, at-most-one occupancy rule, requested count, ten-ship and 400-call limits, both authenticated examples in source order, the first explanation, all four constraint entries, and all three source hints. The source's ans literal in Example 2 is retained exactly.

A fresh authenticated Premium review confirmed two examples, one explanation, four constraint entries, three hints, and no source tables, images, diagrams, notes, or follow-up. source_fidelity.json binds all five modular Reference files to live-content SHA-256 b2a38b5a901f7ecf488a7592339e34dc04356af39a9904c44436ca70bcf27694 and validates without errors.
